doc.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006

title: Why Hamilton and what the Catatonic Five gave him
summary: His dentist father chose Hamilton in 1949; being drummer in the Catatonic Five meant most to him and carried him through a legal career.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: It sounds like a good match of doctors. Good. What brought you to Hamilton in 1949?

’49. My father was a dentist. In those days you didn’t go to a liberal arts college, you just went right to dental school from high school. He had heard about this college and he was so impressed with this campus that he wanted me to come here and brought me up, and I was interviewed by Sid Bennett, the Director of Admissions, and I’m very happy I came here. And one of the happiest things is the Catatonic Five. That was remarkable. I achieved some honors. I was elected the President of my class, selected the President of my fraternity, I was a member of the Student Council, but of all those things it was being the drummer in the Catatonic Five that pleased me the most, and helped me the most the rest of my life.

Lawyering is not always the most pleasant thing to do and I had this pastime of playing drums in jazz bands. And I so enjoyed that that it got me through being a lawyer. Now I’m through being a lawyer and just playing jazz, so I still play in New York every week and with several other bands, so it’s a pleasure. But it was Hamilton College that got me started.
